notes.problem: A flat-front stack centred in an empty violet field. The single gilt edge is a hairline you can't see at 432 px, so the 1-in-200 argument doesn't read, and the left half of the frame is dead.
notes.fix: Shoot the planned 40 cm macro with the stack edge running corner to corner and fanned, so the gilt edge catches the key as a visible gold band in the foreground and the stack fills the frame.

notes.problem: A frontal flat slab of ruled lines in an empty mauve void. The one gilded page is a 2 px line invisible at feed size, half the frame is dead, and the dark wash behind the headline reads as a smudge.
notes.fix: Re-shoot as the planned 40 cm diagonal macro of a slightly fanned stack in a graphite tray, raking key from the left, with the gilded edge fanned out a few mm and lit as the frame's brightest highlight.

notes.problem: The stack is seen flat from the front and spans about 380 of 1080 px against the storyboard's 900. The left half of the frame is dead violet, dark wash blobs sit behind the headline and the body text, and the single gilded edge is an invisible hairline at feed size.
notes.fix: Re-shoot it as the planned 40 cm macro with the stack edge running corner to corner and filling the frame, sheets slightly fanned and raked by a side key so the one gilt edge catches a highlight. Then drop the wash blobs, because the out-of-focus sweep will give the type its quiet.

notes.problem: The cutaway machine, chute and desk sit small in the lower half, seen from high and far, and the top 45% of the frame is type on a wash.
notes.fix: Drop the camera to a lower three-quarter view and push in until the glass housing and the gold page on the chute fill at least half the frame, with the person's lamp pool cropped at the right edge.

notes.problem: 'At least one in four' is not countable at 432 px. The side tray, the ramp page and the engine pages are tiny, the left third is empty pink, and the dark type wash approaches a plate.
notes.fix: Pull the camera in so the engine and fork fill the lower 60 percent, and show four large pages leaving the engine with exactly one riding the gold ramp to the person while three go to the tray.

notes.problem: The cutaway machine, the chute and the reader sit small on a diagonal across a mostly empty rose sweep, so the fork, one page in four rising to a person, doesn't read as one silhouette at 432 px.
notes.fix: Push the camera in until the cutaway housing and chute fill at least half the frame width, and crop the reader's lamp pool off the right edge so the rising gold page is the focal point.

notes.problem: The paper strata texture is streaky and aliased, the slips look pasted on, and the orthographic elevation flattens a relief meant to read as a cliff of weight.
notes.fix: Rotate the relief to a three-quarter raking view with the key from the upper left so each bundle casts onto the next, and replace the streak texture with fine sheet-edge displacement.

notes.problem: The raised 'gold' tiles render salmon pink and sit close in value to the cream unraised tiles, so the 34 of 100 reads as noise rather than a count, and the accent's meaning breaks.
notes.fix: Give the raised tiles the true dusk gold #E0956A in satin metal and drop the cream tiles a step in value, so the 34 raised tiles separate at a glance under the low south-west key.

notes.problem: The desk, chair and chute float small in a wide empty violet sweep. The gold route, the payoff of the bookend, is a thin rail at upper right.
notes.fix: Move the camera in and down so the lit desk and the page landing in the tray fill the middle third, with the chute entering large from the right edge.

notes.problem: A competent but generic drawer macro that repeats the November 16th deck's card drawer. The gold tabs are the only thing that ties it to this story.
notes.fix: Swap the cabinet for this deck's own object, such as one wall of about 3,000 scored answer pages in a sealed glass case beside the engine, so the closed database reads as this machine's, not an archive.

notes.problem: The scorer's foot floats beside the chair arm at about (900,1150), and a stray brown slab sits on the left edge at about (0 to 20, 1500 to 1620).
notes.fix: Re-pose the figure's legs under the desk behind the chair and delete or crop the stray left-edge mesh.

notes.problem: The tallest column leans visibly from lens distortion, there are no kraft ream bands, and the trees are flat dark cards.
notes.fix: Shift-correct the camera (vertical lens shift instead of tilt) so the columns stand plumb, and add kraft bands every 500 sheets so the 2,758 block shows five.
